The strongest ground is that the promise was oral. Many states require a writing signed by the debtor to revive a debt already barred by the statute of limitations, and the common-law rule that a moral obligation supports a new promise does not override that requirement. Lack of consideration is weaker because Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 treats a promise to pay a barred debt as binding without new consideration, and the overheard "deadbeat" remark neither supplies consideration nor creates duress.

CONFIDENCE: 60
